newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* Time Warner Inc plans to announce on Monday that it has begun selling access to the Internet to 400 cable television subscribers in Akron, Ohio.
* California's Silicon Valley is hearing rumours that Jean-Louis Gassee, the former product development and research chief at Apple Computer Inc, may rejoin the company.
* Vanity Fair magazine has slowly rebuilt its circulation and advertising under the lead of E. Graydon Carter, four years after he took over as editor from Tina Brown.
* Supermarket tabloids The Star, The Globe and National Enquirer have each lost about 30 percent of their circulation in the past five years despite gaining some acceptance in the mainstream press.
* James Fallows will begin his tenure as editor of U.S. News & World Report on Monday with significant changes in the magazine's leadership.

* Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide, a unit of WPP Group Plc, has become the first major advertising agency to hand the post of chief executive title from one woman, Charlotte Beers who remains chairwoman, to another, Shelly Lazarus.

* The Federal Small Business Administration's site on the World Wide Web is a successful place for small businesses searching for prospective clients and customers, as the Internet's role in commerce grows.
* Novell Inc will spend $20 million between now and October 31 on a new brand-identity advertising campaign.
